messages:
incident-bot: HIGH alert: sudden spike in 5xx for /v1/streaming and paging endpoints in us-west-2 canary cluster. 30s abnormality detection.

alex (on-call): saw it. looking now. are canaries in the usual flux group? :eyes:

maya (eng-runtime): yep canary pool 03. rolling v10.2.0 -> new streaming frame header change. telemetry shows 'ERR_UNSUPPORTED_FRAME' and 'invalid_frame_version' in logs.

jules (release): that rollout started 02:12 UTC to 10% canary nodes. we gated on integration smoke but not end-to-end streaming paging tests. reassigning.

alex (on-call): sample logs?

maya (eng-runtime): pasted logs:```\n[2026-03-15T02:18:12Z] conn=20345 - decode_error: unsupported frame version 0x7f\n[2026-03-15T02:18:12Z] client=svc-abc - respond 400 {"error":"unsupported_frame_version","expected":"0x01","got":"0x7f"}\n```

samir (eng-platform): metrics: streaming open connections down 18% on canary slice, paging tail latency spikes for clients using client-sdk >=10.0.0. non-canary traffic unaffected so far.

kevin (support): we have 4 customer reports (dedicated + private) with disconnects, one is reporting repeated pagination failures (cursor errors). I've opened a ticket and flagged high.

lena (product): customer impact? are return-to-normal estimates?

alex (on-call): quick triage: looks like client/server frame version mismatch. likely server started accepting a new frame type that old clients don't handle. options: 1) flip kill-switch on feature flag to have server speak legacy frames, 2) emergency rollback of v10.2.0 canary, 3) deploy compatibility shim. Kill-switch fastest.

jules (release): can toggle feature flag 'streaming_frame_v2' via console or api. console toggle takes ~15s to propagate to serving control plane. I can flip now if we agree.

alex (on-call): do it. toggle first, monitor. if still noisy then rollback.

jules (release): toggling now. api: `POST https://ff.redwood.internal/toggle streaming_frame_v2 false --env=canary`

incident-bot: feature-flag toggle initiated by jules at 02:22 UTC. propagation event ID ff-7832.

maya (eng-runtime): seeing config refresh, restarting route workers on canary slice, new config to force legacy frame. tailing logs...

maya (eng-runtime): partial improvement: 5xx rate dropped 60% in 40s but still see occasional ERR_UNSUPPORTED_FRAME on older connections established earlier. connection re-establish should fix.

kevin (support): customers reporting reconnect fixed or transient. updating tickets.

samir (eng-platform): because some connections are sticky, we should do a gradual roll-back of the canary revision to fully restore state. I can trigger rollback to v10.1.3 on canary pool and mark for full halt.

jules (release): initiating canary rollback to v10.1.3 now. command: `rolloutctl rollback --service streaming --to-version 10.1.3 --target canary-03`

incident-bot: rollback started by jules at 02:27 UTC.

alex (on-call): what about clients already upgraded to 10.2.0 in customer infra (private)? do they get errors if server goes back?

maya (eng-runtime): v10.2.0 clients can talk to legacy server if server speaks legacy frame, so toggling kill-switch is safe. full rollback keeps server binary at older version; clients newer shouldn't break as long as server supports legacy frames. main risk was server sending a new frame without fallback.

lena (product): timeline + customer comms: kevin please draft a short note for affected customers — what happened, mitigation, and whether any data loss or degraded tokens.

kevin (support): drafting: "We observed streaming disconnections and paging errors for a subset of requests due to a canary rollout that introduced a new streaming frame version. We reverted the canary and toggled a compatibility flag; customers should see restored connectivity. No data loss; some in-flight streams may have dropped and will need resubmission. Full post-incident with root cause and tests to follow." Will send to affected list after confirmation.

maya (eng-runtime): rollback succeeded on canary-03 at 02:33 UTC. health checks show canary slice back to nominal. 5xxs down to baseline. paging latency normalized.

jules (release): halting further rollouts and locking release branch v10.2.0. moving to patch release candidate.

alex (on-call): marking incident mitigated. moving to RCA phase. handoff to maya/samir/jules for deep dive. I'll update on-call rota and incident channel. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: incident state changed to MITIGATED by alex at 02:36 UTC. duration 24 minutes.

lena (product): please include customer impact numbers: how many distinct customers affected, which tiers, and whether Dedicated/Private were disproportionately hit.

samir (eng-platform): preliminary: 4 customers reported directly; telemetry shows ~0.8% of streaming sessions from canary slice failed; private deployments that pulled 10.2.0 clients experienced disconnects until flag toggle. No Dedicated hosted customers on stable had issues.

kevin (support): sent customer note to affected customers at 02:45 UTC.

alex (on-call): next steps: 1) release team to cut 10.2.1 patch that includes compatibility checks + e2e streaming paging tests; 2) infra to add forced reconnect on frame-version mismatch with clearer error to customers; 3) product to update rollout checklist to include streaming e2e canary harness.

maya (eng-runtime): adding logs to PR that detect frame header mismatch and attach connection id. sample quickfix snippet we've landed in canary to improve observability:```\nif (frame_version != EXPECTED) {\n  log.warn("frame_mismatch", {conn, expected: EXPECTED, got: frame_version});\n  close_conn_with_code(conn, "ERR_UNSUPPORTED_FRAME");\n}\n```

jules (release): also adding an automatic kill-switch alarm whenever 5xx > baseline*4 for 1m during rollout.

alex (on-call): thanks team. I'll file the incident ticket and assign RCA owners. closing thread but will follow up with postmortem draft. :memo:

incident-bot: thread closed for new activity by alex at 03:05 UTC.
